meta.title: Daymark
meta.description: Try Daymark in a throwaway WordPress. Opens the Daymark app with sample Marks and four sites already followed.
meta.author: jeffpaul

steps.code:
<?php
require_once '/wordpress/wp-load.php';

if ( ! class_exists( 'Daymark_Plugin' ) ) {
	return;
}

$plugin = Daymark_Plugin::instance();

// A new WordPress comes with a "Hello world!" post. Take it out, so the
// Timeline opens on the demo.
$hello = get_page_by_path( 'hello-world', OBJECT, 'post' );
if ( $hello instanceof WP_Post ) {
	wp_delete_post( $hello->ID, true );
}

// The same four sites the README's "Try it" demo follows
// (.github/blueprints/blueprint.json). Keep the two lists the same.
$preset_sites = [
	'https://jeffpaul.com'    => 'Jeffrey Paul',
	'https://jondesrosiers.com' => '',
	'https://aaron.jorb.in'  => 'Aaron Jorbin',
	'https://xkcd.com'        => 'xkcd',
];

foreach ( $preset_sites as $site_url => $site_name ) {
	$result = $plugin->subscriptions->subscribe_to_site( $site_url );
	if ( ! is_wp_error( $result ) ) {
		if ( '' !== $site_name ) {
			$plugin->subscriptions->update( (int) $result, [ 'site_title' => $site_name ] );
		}
		$plugin->subscription_poller->poll_subscription( (int) $result );
	}
}

// Sample Marks, one for each Mark type and Featured Content kind. The
// released plugin does not carry the script, so an earlier step copied it
// (and the sample photos next to it) here.
$seed = WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/daymark-demo/seed-sample-content.php';
if ( file_exists( $seed ) ) {
	require $seed;
}
